findings.title: load() silently parses an existing file with an unsupported extension as delimiter-sniffed CSV, returning garbage instead of an error
findings.repro:
import pathlib; import hypertools as hyp
p = pathlib.Path('/tmp/junk.xyz'); p.write_text('hello')
print(repr(hyp.load(str(p))))
findings.expected: HypertoolsIOError (or ValueError) naming the unsupported extension '.xyz' and listing supported formats
findings.actual:
Empty DataFrame
Columns: [he, Unnamed: 1, o]
Index: []   (no exception, no warning)

findings.title: predict() on empty/degenerate data silently returns nonsense forecasts instead of erroring
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
print(hyp.predict(np.array([]), t=5).shape)
print(hyp.predict(5, t=2).shape)
findings.expected: ValueError: input has no observations (or 'need >= 2 observations to forecast')
findings.actual: predict-empty -> OK DataFrame(5, 0); predict-scalar -> OK DataFrame(2, 1) (no exception, no warning)

findings.title: align() and impute() silently swallow misspelled constructor kwargs (documented **kwargs passthrough), returning default-parameter results
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
RNG = np.random.RandomState(0); X = RNG.rand(20,4); Y = RNG.rand(20,4)
XNAN = X.copy(); XNAN[2,1] = np.nan
print(np.allclose(np.asarray(hyp.align([X,Y])[0]), np.asarray(hyp.align([X,Y], n_itr=5)[0])))  # True -> typo ignored
d = np.asarray(hyp.impute(XNAN, model='SimpleImputer'))
t = np.asarray(hyp.impute(XNAN, model='SimpleImputer', stratgy='median'))
print(np.allclose(d, t))  # True -> typo ignored
findings.expected: TypeError: ... got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_itr' / 'stratgy' (as predict and manip already raise)
findings.actual: ALIGN typo n_itr=5 == default (silently ignored if True): True; impute typo stratgy == default (silently ignored): True; align-bogus-kwarg -> OK list(len=2); impute-bogus-kwarg -> OK DataFrame(20, 4)

findings.title: None input: manip/predict/impute crash with raw third-party internals and analyze silently returns None, while the rest of the API gives a clear TypeError
findings.expected: the same clear TypeError ('Unsupported data type passed...') from every function
findings.actual: manip -> IndexError: list index out of range [datawrangler/decorate/decorate.py:467]; predict -> ValueError: negative dimensions are not allowed [pykalman/standard.py:533]; impute -> ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity [numpy]; analyze -> None (silent); reduce -> TypeError: Unsupported data type passed. Supported types: ...

findings.title: Empty-list input to align/manip/impute/predict is misrouted into the TEXT-embedding pipeline: loads the minipedia corpus, prints to stdout, then crashes with an LDA shape error
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.align([])
findings.expected: ValueError: input has no observations (0 rows); there is nothing to plot or analyze. (as reduce/cluster/normalize/plot already raise)
findings.actual: stdout: 'loading corpus: minipedia...done!' then ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation. [sklearn/utils/validation.py:1097]

findings.title: load('sotus') returns a fitted sklearn Pipeline instead of the documented State of the Union speeches (docstring claim fails on recompute)
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
s = hyp.load('sotus'); print(type(s))
findings.expected: a text collection (list/DataFrame of 30 SOTU speeches, 1989-2018)
findings.actual: <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'> | warnings: InconsistentVersionWarning x3; cached payload at ~/hypertools_data/sotus is a pickled sklearn Pipeline

findings.title: manip Resample: n_samples=0 silently returns an EMPTY dataset; negative/float n_samples leak numpy internals -- while plot(resample=...) validates the same concept properly
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.rand(20, 4)
print(hyp.manip(X, model='Resample', n_samples=0).shape)  # (0, 4), silent
hyp.manip(X, model='Resample', n_samples=7.5)  # cryptic TypeError
findings.expected: ValueError: n_samples must be an integer >= 2 ... (mirroring plot's resample= message)
findings.actual: n_samples=0 -> OK DataFrame(0, 4); n_samples=-10 -> ValueError: Number of samples, -10, must be non-negative. [numpy function_base.py:124]; n_samples=7.5 -> TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer [numpy function_base.py:122]

findings.title: normalize= spec validation uses AssertionError, names the internal 'scale_type' instead of the public kwarg, and is silently case-sensitive
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.normalize(np.random.rand(20, 4), normalize='ACROSS')
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize= must be one of 'across', 'within', 'row' (case-sensitive), False/None, or a fitted Normalizer; got 'ACROSS'
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer. [tools/normalize.py:240]

findings.title: Smooth kernel_width validation is inconsistent and its message is inaccurate: claims 'positive odd integer' but accepts 10 and 4.5; 0 vs -5 raise different exception classes
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.rand(20, 4)
print(np.asarray(hyp.manip(X, model='Smooth', kernel_width=10)).shape)   # accepted
print(np.asarray(hyp.manip(X, model='Smooth', kernel_width=4.5)).shape)  # accepted
hyp.manip(X, model='Smooth', kernel_width=-5)  # AssertionError 'positive odd integer'
findings.expected: one consistent ValueError describing the ACTUAL accepted domain
findings.actual: kernel_width=10 -> OK (20, 4); kernel_width=4.5 -> OK (20, 4); kernel_width=-5 -> AssertionError: smoothing kernel width must be a positive odd integer; kernel_width=0 -> ValueError: the savgol kernel needs kernel_width (1) > order (3); ...

findings.title: The same invalid model spec (model=42 / model=True) produces three different exception behaviors across the dispatchers
findings.expected: the same ValueError shape everywhere: 'unknown <stage> model 42; supported names: ... (or pass a class/instance/dict spec)'
findings.actual: reduce -> ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options...; cluster -> AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'fit'; align/manip/impute -> ValueError: unknown model: 42

findings.title: reduce is the only dispatcher whose unknown-model error doesn't list the supported names; it points to a legacy 0.8 docs URL instead
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(20, 4), reduce='NotARealModel')
findings.expected: ValueError: unknown reduce model 'NotARealModel'; supported names: PCA, IncrementalPCA, ... (matching the other dispatchers)
findings.actual: ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce [reduce/reduce.py:237]

findings.title: Invalid n_clusters leaks sklearn's InvalidParameterError class through cluster()/plot() instead of a hypertools-level ValueError
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.cluster(np.random.rand(20, 4), n_clusters=0)
findings.expected: ValueError: n_clusters must be an integer >= 1; got 0
findings.actual: sklearn.utils._param_validation.InvalidParameterError: The 'n_clusters' parameter of KMeans must be an int in the range [1, inf). Got 0 instead. [sklearn/utils/_param_validation.py:98]

findings.title: plot fmt list length mismatch crashes with bare IndexError -- fmt missed the GH #206 per-dataset length validation that color/marker/linestyle received
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.rand(20, 4); Y = np.random.rand(20, 4)
hyp.plot([X, Y], ['r-'], show=False)
findings.expected: ValueError: fmt= was given as a list of length 1, but there are 2 dataset(s) to plot ... (like color/marker/linestyle)
findings.actual: IndexError: list index out of range [plot/plot.py:2333]

findings.title: Animation kwargs validated lazily or not at all: rotations='two' only crashes at SAVE time deep in matplotlib; duration=-5 crashes STATIC plots with a numpy reduction error; zoom=-1 silently accepted
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.rand(20, 4)
hyp.plot(X, duration=-5, show=False)  # static plot, cryptic numpy error
# and:
# out = hyp.plot(X, animate=True, rotations='two', duration=0.2, frame_rate=10, save_path='/tmp/r.gif', show=False)
findings.expected: eager ValueError naming rotations/duration and the accepted domain
findings.actual: static duration=-5 -> ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity; rotations='two' + save -> IndexError: list index out of range [matplotlib/animation.py:506]; zoom=-1 -> OK silently

findings.title: Cryptic low-level errors for wrong-typed plot kwargs: ax=, size=, transform=, matrix hue= with 3 dims, morph_samples=, fmt=int
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.rand(20, 4)
hyp.plot(X, ax='myaxis', show=False)
findings.expected: ValueError/TypeError naming the kwarg and its accepted form (e.g. 'ax= must be a matplotlib Axes; got str')
findings.actual: ax='myaxis' -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'name' [plot/plot.py:1562]; size=[4,4,4] -> ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2) [matplotlib/figure.py:3139]; transform='banana' -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'shape'; hue 3-D -> TypeError: unhashable type: 'numpy.ndarray'; morph_samples=-5 -> ValueError: negative dimensions are not allowed [numpy]; fmt=123 -> TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable

findings.title: plot silently accepts inconsistent labels/hue/legend inputs: short labels list labels a subset with no warning; string hue and int legend silently 'work'
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.RandomState(0).rand(20, 4)
fig = hyp.plot(X, labels=['only-label'], show=False)
print(len(fig.axes[0].texts))  # 1, silently
findings.expected: ValueError for mismatched labels length (mirroring hue's message); TypeError/ValueError for non-list/array hue and non-bool/list legend
findings.actual: labels=[1 entry] on 20 points -> 1 annotation, no warning; hue='notacolumn' -> OK single-color figure; legend=7 -> OK Figure

findings.title: describe() returns empty results silently for degenerate max_dims/1-column data; float max_dims crashes with a bare TypeError
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
print(hyp.describe(np.random.rand(20, 4), max_dims=0, show=False))
hyp.describe(np.random.rand(20, 4), max_dims=2.5, show=False)
findings.expected: ValueError: max_dims must be an integer >= 2; got 0 (and a clear error for 1-column input)
findings.actual: max_dims=0/-3/1-col -> {'average': [], 'individual': [[]]} silently; max_dims=2.5 -> TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer [reduce/describe.py:110]; describe(X, show=False, backend='bogus') -> OK

findings.title: ndims larger than the data's feature count is silently capped with no warning (even for explicit PCA); apply_model(ndims=0) silently returns width-0 data
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.rand(20, 4)
print(hyp.reduce(X, reduce='PCA', ndims=10).shape)  # (20, 4), silent
print(hyp.apply_model(X, 'PCA', ndims=0).shape)     # (20, 0), silent
findings.expected: UserWarning when capping ndims to n_features; ValueError for ndims=0 via apply_model (matching reduce)
findings.actual: reduce(X, 'PCA', ndims=10) -> (20, 4) no warning; apply_model(X, 'PCA', ndims=0) -> (20, 0) no error

findings.title: align SRM with features=-1 leaks numpy's 'negative dimensions are not allowed' from inside random-state internals
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.rand(20, 4); Y = np.random.rand(20, 4)
hyp.align([X, Y], model='SRM', features=-1)
findings.expected: ValueError: features must be a positive integer; got -1
findings.actual: ValueError: negative dimensions are not allowed [numpy/random/_common.pyx:310]

findings.title: predict() with too few observations crashes with a pykalman broadcast error instead of stating the minimum data requirement
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.predict(np.random.rand(1, 4), t=5)
findings.expected: ValueError: Kalman forecasting requires at least 2 observations; got 1
findings.actual: ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (4,4) into shape (4,1) [pykalman/standard.py:400]

findings.title: load(42) / load(None) raise the raw os.fspath TypeError with no hypertools context
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.load(123)
findings.expected: TypeError: dataset must be a string (dataset name, path, or URL) or a list of strings; got int
findings.actual: TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not int

findings.title: save() rough edges: an int fname is treated as an OS file descriptor (OSError Errno 9 -- or a silent write to an unrelated open fd); unpicklable objects raise a bare pickle error; the docstring is a single line
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.random.rand(3, 3), 42)
findings.expected: TypeError: fname must be a string path; got int
findings.actual: OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor [io/save.py:21]; save(<lambda>, path) -> AttributeError: Can't get local object '<lambda>.<locals>.<lambda>' [io/save.py:22]

findings.title: impute() cannot describe its own core failure mode: all-NaN input dies with a numpy reduction error instead of 'input is entirely missing'
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.impute(np.full((10, 3), np.nan))
findings.expected: ValueError: input is entirely missing (all values are NaN); there is nothing to impute
findings.actual: ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity [numpy/_core/fromnumeric.py:86]

findings.title: load() docstring dataset descriptions do not match reality: 'spiral' is a list of two arrays (not 'a numpy array'); 'mushroomm' typo
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d = hyp.load('spiral'); print(type(d), len(d), np.asarray(d[0]).shape)
findings.expected: docstring describing a list of two (1000, 3) arrays
findings.actual: load('spiral') -> list of 2 arrays, each (1000, 3); docstring says 'is numpy array containing data for a 3D spiral'

findings.title: analyze() with no stage kwargs silently passes ANY input through untouched (analyze(None) -> None); pipeline= of the wrong type raises a bare AttributeError
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
print(hyp.analyze(None))  # None, silently
hyp.analyze([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]], pipeline='notapipeline')
findings.expected: the standard input-validation TypeError; and ValueError: pipeline= must be a fitted hypertools.Pipeline; got str
findings.actual: analyze(None) -> None (silent); analyze(X, pipeline='notapipeline') -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'transform' [tools/analyze.py:141]

findings.title: Pipeline constructor edge cases: a bare string is iterated character-wise ('unknown pipeline step 'P''), an int step defers failure to fit time, None crashes with a bare TypeError
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.Pipeline('PCA')
findings.expected: ValueError: steps must be a list (got the string 'PCA' -- did you mean Pipeline(['PCA'])?)
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown pipeline step 'P'; supported names: AffinityPropagation, ... ; Pipeline([42]) -> OK (deferred failure); Pipeline(None) -> TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable

findings.title: Datasets with mismatched column counts crash reduce/plot with numpy's raw vstack message instead of naming the ragged datasets
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.reduce([np.random.rand(20, 4), np.random.rand(20, 3)], ndims=2)
findings.expected: ValueError: datasets must share the same number of features to be stacked; dataset 0 has 4, dataset 1 has 3 (consider hyp.align)
findings.actual: ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 4 and the array at index 1 has size 3 [numpy/_core/shape_base.py:292]
